resources.string: EnforceDoze tunes Android\'s Doze so the phone sleeps deeper with the screen off. It keeps its own log of every night and shows whether Doze held, with the numbers.
Nothing changes until you apply a plan, and Restore stock puts everything back.
It runs as the shell user, so EnforceDoze can apply every lever and read them back.
It runs as root, so EnforceDoze can apply every lever and read them back.
Allow EnforceDoze to use it: the worker it starts runs the Doze commands and nothing else.
Changing Doze needs a helper running as the shell user. On Android 17 the official Shizuku 13.6.0 cannot allow new apps. Any of these works:
Forks that keep Shizuku\'s protocol work the same way. Reported working on Android 17 as of November 2026: thedjchi/Shizuku, Nightzuku and Shizuku+. None is endorsed; check before you install.
On a rooted phone, the Sui module does the same job.
If Shizuku runs but its dialog never opens, grant the permission from a computer, then restart Shizuku:
Grant read access once from a computer. EnforceDoze then reads Doze and keeps its log, but cannot change anything:
Your answer decides how far the plan may delay ordinary messages. Alarms and calls are never delayed.
The plan keeps Doze gentle and adds no night profile.
A short wait is fine. Most people pick this.
Messages can wait until you pick the phone up.
The phone holds no screen-off time to learn from. Everyday is a safe start; Recommended refines after the first night.
Read-only: the plan shows, but applying it needs Shizuku, Sui or root.
Applied. It runs from now on.
See it work, in two minutes
Quick proof runs the levers for real while you watch: it applies the timings, forces deep idle with the phone unplugged in software, restricts sensors, reads each one back, then undoes it all.
Quick proof needs Shizuku, Sui or root. You can run it later from Home.
